_note: Glossary shown on the home page. Plain-English definitions for non-specialists.

glossary.def: A doughnut-shaped fusion reactor that holds its plasma in place with magnetic fields.
Gas heated so far that its atoms split into charged particles. Fusion fuel is a plasma of about 150 million °C.
A material that carries electric current with no resistance once it is cooled far enough. Fusion magnets are wound from superconductors.
"Rare-earth barium copper oxide": the high-temperature superconductor used in compact fusion magnets. It is a thin metal tape coated in layers; the rare earth is usually yttrium or gadolinium.
Niobium-tin wire: the low-temperature superconductor used in ITER-style magnets.
A group of 17 metals, including yttrium, used in magnets and electronics. Heavy rare earths are mined mainly from clay deposits in southern China and Myanmar.
The processing step that turns ore into pure metal or oxide. Ore from many mines is mixed here, which is where its origin is usually lost.
Any step where material from different sources is mixed, so a buyer further down the chain can no longer tell which mine it came from.
A database of company registries, ownership, sanctions lists and customs records. This site uses it to show who trades with whom.
A confirmed link rests on a specific record, such as a shipment or a registry filing. An inferred link is modelled or assumed from market structure.
Tin, tantalum, tungsten and gold: minerals that US and EU rules single out because their trade has financed armed groups.
Legal restrictions on dealing with named people or companies. OFAC is the US Treasury office that keeps the main US list.
